item.title: FusionGaussian: Incremental 3-D Gaussian Splatting for Large-Scale Aerial Photogrammetry
item.description: Large-scale unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photogrammetry is essential for geospatial modeling, where 3-D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) has recently shown transformative potential for high-fidelity reconstruction. However, existing 3DGS frameworks for large-scale scenes often rely on static partitioning and lack the flexibility needed for incremental expansion. When updating models with multimission data, these methods incur prohibitive computational costs for global retraining and exhibit geometric inconsistencies at fusion boundaries. To address these limitations, we propose FusionGaussian, a novel framework for scalable and incremental scene reconstruction based on 3DGS. Our approach enables independent training of subscenes captured from different UAV missions and supports incremental integration without global retraining. Specifically, we incorporate an overlap-aware view selection and boundary refinement strategy to address insufficient supervision in boundary regions, along with a blockwise competitive merging mechanism to improve rendering quality and geometric consistency during scene fusion. Extensive experiments on four real-world UAV datasets and two temporal update case studies demonstrate that FusionGaussian consistently outperforms direct-merge incremental baselines in rendering and geometric quality, particularly in overlapping regions, while achieving competitive full-scene quality and substantially lower cumulative reconstruction cost than repeated Global-All reconstruction.
item.authors: Zhenyu Xia;Pengcheng Han;Lin Chen;Boni Hu;Shuhui Bu;

item.title: LPFI-Net: A Fusion Network for LiDAR Prior and Frequency Interaction in Hyperspectral and LiDAR Classification
item.description: The integration of multisource information from hyperspectral imagery (HSI) and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) provides reliable data support for land cover classification. The heterogeneity between HSI and LiDAR data poses significant challenges for cross-modal feature alignment, while the rich structural priors inherent in LiDAR data remain underutilized. Therefore, significant feature alignment learning between HSI and LiDAR, together with the embedding of LiDAR structural priors, can substantially improve land cover classification performance. Based on these, we propose the LiDAR prior and frequency interaction network (LPFI-Net). LPFI-Net employs frequency-domain feature learning to achieve flexible HSI-LiDAR salient feature alignment. A frequency-domain interaction mechanism, together with a frequency-invertible enhancement module, is introduced to strengthen cross-band representations and improve HSI-LiDAR feature reconstruction. In the spatial–frequency fusion stage, a LiDAR structural prior-guided mechanism transforms spatial information into quantifiable priors, enabling more effective cross-modal feature enhancement. Experiments on the Houston2013, MUUFL, and Augsburg datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of LPFI-Net, with code available online.
item.authors: Yuqing Zhao;Yu Song;Chao Liang;Kang Ni;

item.title: Multihierarchical Mixed Cube Attention Interactive Network for Hyperspectral and Multispectral Image Fusion
item.description: To address the tradeoff between the spectral resolution and spatial resolution of hyperspectral images (HSIs), hyperspectral and multispectral image fusion (HSI-MSI) aims to generate a high-spatial-resolution hyperspectral image (HR-HSI) by integrating the spectral information of a hyperspectral image with the spatial details of a corresponding multispectral image (MSI). However, most existing methods overlook the inherent correlation between the spatial and spectral dimensions, limiting their joint exploitation of spatial and spectral information. In this study, a multihierarchical mixed cube attention interactive network (MMCAI-Net) is proposed, which considers this correlation and enhances the deep interaction across spatial and spectral dimensions in the HSI-MSI fusion process. The network primarily consists of a multihierarchical feature interaction stage and a gradual feature reconstruction stage, which are composed of the mixed cube attention interaction (MCAI) and cube feature aggregation and reconstruction (CFAR) modules, respectively. The MCAI module integrates global spatial and spectral information from the HSI and MSI through mixed cube attention, enabling cross-dimensional feature interaction. The CFAR module progressively aggregates these features to reconstruct an HR-HSI with enhanced spatial details and spectral fidelity. Experimental results on five datasets demonstrate that the MMCAI-Net method preserves more spatial and spectral details than seven literature methods, improving PSNR by 5% and reducing SAM by 8% compared with MCT-Net. These results suggest that the proposed method achieves superior HSI-MSI fusion results.
item.authors: Huajing Wu;Wenjing Zhang;Kefei Zhang;Shuangshuang Shi;Fei Zhao;Lin Zhang;Lorenzo Bruzzone;

item.title: QL-Sec: Quantum AI-Enabled Security Framework for LLM-Driven Low-Altitude Remote Sensing Networks
item.description: Low-altitude remote sensing network technology has advanced rapidly, especially with the assistance of large language models (LLMs). The use of LLMs, especially with autonomous aerial vehicles in remote sensing systems, poses significant security and privacy risks due to the need to transmit sensitive information and to enable large-scale distributed communication. This article introduces the quantum AI security (QL-Sec) framework for LLM-powered low-altitude remote sensing networks. The proposed solution utilizes a hybrid QL-Sec mechanism designed to enhance confidentiality, integrity, and authentication, and to resist adversarial intrusions. The framework also uses quantum-secured encryption and privacy-preserving feature perturbation to help reduce information leakage during edge–cloud communication. Results reveal that the proposed framework achieves 96.41% attack detection accuracy, a secret key rate of 0.91 bits/use, and a reduced quantum bit error rate of 0.029. Shapley additive explanations explainability analysis validates the contribution of quantum-secure and quantum-safe components to trustworthy decision-making. The proposed quantum AI-based system provides an efficient, scalable, and highly secure solution for future intelligent low-altitude remote sensing systems.
item.authors: Wajdan Al Malwi;Hussam Al Hamadi;Abdulrahman Mohammed Alamoudi;Nazik Alturki;Fatima Asiri;Fahad Masood;

item.title: Adversarial Patch Attack on Ship Detection via Localized Data Augmentation
item.description: Current ship detection techniques based on remote sensing imagery primarily rely on the object detection capabilities of deep neural networks (DNNs). However, DNNs are vulnerable to adversarial patch attacks, which can deceive the detection model and lead to misclassifications. Numerous studies have demonstrated that data augmentation-based methods can improve the transferability of adversarial patches. However, excessive augmentation of image backgrounds or irrelevant regions may introduce unnecessary interference, which also resulting in false detections of the detection models. When using such kind of loss to optimize the adversarial patches, it will inevitably lead to the optimization direction deviating from correct track, because these loss are not caused by the adversarial patches themselves but rather by the overaugmentation of background and nontarget areas. Therefore, this article proposes a localized data augmentation method that applies augmentation only to the target regions, avoiding any influence on nontarget areas. By reducing background interference, this approach enables the loss function to focus more directly on the impact of the adversarial patches on the detection model, thereby improving the attack success rate. Experiments conducted on the HRSC2016 dataset have confirmed our hypotheses. When compared with the baselines, including the global data augmentation based method, the proposed method shows the ability to increase the attack success rate of adversarial patches and enhance their transferability across different object detection models.
item.authors: Chun Liu;Panpan Ding;Zheng Zheng;Hailong Wang;Bingqian Zhu;Tao Xu;Guangxia Wang;

item.title: FireAURA-Net: Progressive Candidate-Aware Representation and Localization for Tiny Forest-Fire Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
item.description: Detecting tiny forest fire points in remote sensing imagery is challenging due to their low pixel occupancy, weak responses, irregular boundaries, and similarity to fire-like woodland backgrounds. Limited task-specific training data further exacerbate representation insufficiency and foreground–background imbalance. In this article, we propose an adaptive unified response alignment network for tiny forest-fire detection (FireAURA-Net), a lightweight detector. Local-context contrast-guided response mining preserves weak candidates through local-context contrast, shallow spatial guidance, and sparse top-$k$ selection. HSV–Semantic Heterogeneous Representation Collaborative Fusion exploits the consistency and discrepancy between an explicit HSV color prior and candidate semantic responses to improve candidate reliability under fire-like interference. Candidate-localization consistency-guided selective localization refinement block establishes bidirectional interaction between fine-grained candidate cues and deep localization semantics for cross-level refinement. Adaptive dual-cue dynamic reweighting combines target-scale and high-response background cues with weight ramp-up and a batch-level budget constraint to stabilize classification under foreground sparsity. Among the compared methods, FireAURA-Net achieves the highest $\text{AP}$, $\text{AP}_{75}$, and $\text{AP}_{\mathrm{s}}$ of 0.193, 0.091, and 0.149, respectively, on forest imagery for remote sensing evaluation of small fire targets, and the highest $\text{AP}_{75}$ and $\text{AP}_{\mathrm{s}}$ of 0.669 and 0.418, respectively, on UAVs-FFDB. These results demonstrate competitive overall detection performance and consistent advantages in detection at $\text{IoU}=0.75$ and in small-scale fire-point detection. Ablation experiments further support the modules' contributions.
item.authors: Yuhan Liu;Hongyang Zhao;Tao Jiang;Jiayi Sun;Yi Liu;Jing Jin;

item.title: Reliability-Enhanced State-Space Interaction for Robust Remote Sensing Change Detection
item.description: Remote sensing change detection aims to identify land-cover changes from bitemporal images acquired over the same area. Although existing deep learning methods have achieved promising performance, they still suffer from pseudochanges caused by illumination variation, seasonal difference, shadows, sensor inconsistency, and slight spatial misalignment. Moreover, most bitemporal interaction strategies propagate temporal discrepancies without explicitly judging their reliability, which may amplify appearance-induced perturbations as change cues. To address these issues, we propose a reliability-aware change-guided state-space interaction framework for robust remote sensing change detection. Specifically, we first use temporal-consistent feature preparation (TCFP) to produce temporally comparable and locally refined hierarchical features. Then, a reliability-enhanced change-guided interaction module is designed to estimate change-evidence reliability and appearance-perturbation uncertainty from complementary state-space discrepancy representations. These reliability measurements are further introduced into the selective state-space interaction to regulate state writing, reading, and updating during bitemporal feature propagation. Finally, a lightweight hierarchical decoder combines the fused change representations and TCFP-prepared temporal detail cues to generate the final change map. Extensive experiments on six benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving intersection over union/F1 scores of 90.61%/95.07%, 84.29%/91.48%, 90.39%/94.95%, 55.75%/71.59%, 91.67%/95.65%, and 53.50%/69.71% on BCDD, LEVIR-CD, GoogleBuilding, CLCD, DSIFN, and SECOND, respectively.
item.authors: Anbin Yu;

item.title: SARShipRES: A Scattering-Aware Dataset and Structure-Regularized Framework for Referring SAR Ship Segmentation
item.description: Accurately localizing and segmenting user-specified ships in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is essential for maritime surveillance, traffic monitoring, and interactive ocean observation. Referring expression segmentation (RES) provides a flexible language-guided paradigm for target selection; however, existing RES methods are mainly developed for natural images and are difficult to directly transfer to SAR scenarios due to the scattering-dominated imaging mechanism, speckle noise, cluttered nearshore backgrounds, and ambiguous object boundaries. Moreover, most existing RES datasets assume a one-to-one correspondence between an expression and a single target, which is inconsistent with practical maritime interpretation, where a user may refer to multiple ships sharing similar spatial or scattering properties. To address these issues, we present SARShipRES, a SAR-specific referring ship segmentation dataset that integrates spatial, area, semantic, and scattering-aware descriptions and supports both one-to-one and one-to-many image–text–mask annotations. Based on this dataset, we propose a SAM-based multimodal segmentation framework tailored to SAR imaging characteristics. The proposed method introduces a decoder-level scatter-suppressed topological mask refinement strategy to reduce nonstructural bright scatterers, enhance region connectivity, and alleviate fragmented predictions. In addition, an adaptive boundary-aware shape regularization scheme is designed to improve boundary smoothness and geometric consistency while avoiding overregularization of small targets. Extensive experiments under both inshore and offshore conditions demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms representative RES baselines.
item.authors: Yixuan Lv;Furui Chen;Zhuang Zhou;Han Wang;Yuxuan Liu;You Song;

item.title: Lower Boundary-Aware Sky–Ground Segmentation for Robust Horizon Estimation in Low-Altitude UAV Remote Sensing
item.description: Low-altitude uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) provide flexible platforms for remote-sensing data acquisition, but their image sequences are frequently affected by attitude variation, illumination degradation, cluttered sky–ground structures, and partial occlusion. To improve horizon perception under these conditions, this article proposes LBA-YOLO-Seg, a lightweight lower boundary-aware sky–ground segmentation framework that explicitly links mask prediction with downstream geometric recoverability. The method combines Ghost-based feature extraction, Coordinate Attention, and a high-resolution boundary pathway to preserve boundary localization and directional continuity, while a boundary–completeness–adaptive Kalman estimator improves temporal stability. Experiments on a self-collected UAV dataset show that the proposed method outperforms traditional horizon detectors, representative segmentation networks, boundary-aware methods, and YOLO-family baselines in geometric accuracy and temporal stability. Zero-shot evaluation on the public CH1 dataset further demonstrates cross-domain generalization, while embedded deployment on Rhino Pi-X1 achieves an end-to-end processing rate of 47.53 FPS. These results indicate that optimizing segmentation representation for lower boundary recoverability provides an effective and deployable solution for robust UAV horizon perception.
item.authors: Haonan Zhang;Wenyi Lin;Chuandong Guo;Lijia Cao;Huali Gou;Jiajun Li;Jinhui Li;

item.title: Adaptive Multiobjective Pulse Compression for SAR Imaging
item.description: For synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging, the classical matched filter produces high sidelobes that bury weak targets, while windowing sacrifices resolution. Existing mismatched filter designs and adaptive pulse compression methods tend to concentrate on local sidelobe suppression or adopt restricted optimization criteria, resulting in insufficient global control and limited practical effectiveness. To address these issues, a cascaded framework that combines mainlobe-fidelity dual-norm iterative reweighted suppression (MDIRS) with local normalized sharpening (LNS) is proposed. The proposed MDIRS–LNS chain achieves high dynamic range, enhanced weak-target visibility, and a resolution comparable to the matched filter, while attaining a balance between sidelobe suppression depth and resolution retention compared with conventional linear mismatched filters and windowed matched filters. Experiments on simulated and real satellite SAR imagery data are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
item.authors: Jianyuan Li;Pengbo Wang;Wei Liu;Jie Chen;Zhirong Men;

item.title: Frequency-Relation Guided Historical Inversion for Raw-Exemplar-Free Continual Hyperspectral Image Classification
item.description: Raw-exemplar-free continual hyperspectral image (HSI) classification aims to learn newly introduced land-cover classes while retaining old-class discrimination without storing historical HSI patches. In this work, raw-exemplar-free denotes a compact-memory-assisted setting in which no historical HSI patches, pixel-level spectral-spatial tensors, spatial coordinates, or persistent generated samples are retained; only compact noninput statistics and normalized feature references are used for reconstruction guidance and memory calibration. The main challenge is to construct historical evidence that is structurally faithful, discriminative, and consistent with the evolving feature space. To address this challenge, this article proposes a frequency-relation guided structured historical inversion framework, termed FR-SHI. Frequency-relation guided historical reconstruction reconstructs old-class auxiliary samples by combining frequency structural constraints with relation-memory guidance. Old-new collaborative relational distillation preserves both output responses and channel-spatial feature relations of the previous model, while temporal drift suppression and calibration suppresses representation drift and calibrates compact historical memories after each task. Experiments on Houston, Salinas, and WHU-Hi-LongKou show that FR-SHI provides more stable old-class retention and better final classification performance than representative raw-exemplar-free continual learning methods. Compared with the closest raw-exemplar-free HSI-specific inversion baseline, HyperSC, FR-SHI improves final OA by 3.58, 0.88, and 3.91 percentage points on Houston, Salinas, and WHU-Hi-LongKou, respectively.

item.title: Spectral–Spatial Collaborative Calibration for Multisource Domain-Adaptive Semantic Segmentation of Remote Sensing Images
item.description: Multisource unsupervised domain adaptation (MS-UDA) can reduce the annotation burden of remote sensing semantic segmentation, but heterogeneous source spectra and ground sampling distances can destabilize target pseudolabels. This article presents a spectral–spatial collaborative calibration network (SSCCNet) for MS-UDA with RGB and infrared–red–green (IRRG) imagery. First, spectral adaptive normalization (SANM) performs category-conditioned statistical matching from the near-infrared channel of a labeled nonreference source to the red-channel statistics of an RGB reference source, while weak blending preserves source-specific contrast. Second, spatial granularity alignment filtering (SAF) provides resolution-aware contextual compensation for the lower-resolution Vaihingen branch through gated fusion of identity and dilated-convolution responses. Third, dual-threshold filtering (DTF) constructs detached pseudolabels from the current network, combining posterior-confidence screening with a restricted set of near-infrared intensity checks and class-aware weights. Experiments are conducted on two adaptation tasks constructed from ISPRS Potsdam RGB, Potsdam IRRG, and Vaihingen IRRG data. SSCCNet obtains mIoU/OA scores of 40.53%/64.00% and 57.82%/79.36% on the two tasks, respectively. In the cumulative ablation, performance increases at each stage as SANM, SAF, and DTF are introduced in sequence.
item.authors: Xin Li;Zhihao Shi;Xin Lyu;Yihan Niu;Yanan Liu;Jiaxin Li;Yiwei Fang;Chengyi Shi;Hongmin Gao;

item.title: Ensemble-EA and HS-SEA: Attention-Based Efficient Architectures With Bayesian Hyperparameter Optimization for RGB and Hyperspectral Remote Sensing Image Classification
item.description: Conventional deep learning models still face challenges from substantial intra-class variability, complex spatial structures, inter-class similarity, and high spectral dimensionality in hyperspectral imagery. To address these limitations, a unified remote sensing classification framework is proposed consisting of two complementary architectures: Ensemble-EA for RGB aerial scene classification and HS-SEA for hyperspectral image classification. The Ensemble-EA architecture integrates a truncated EfficientNet-B0 backbone, a self-attention mechanism, hierarchical feature learning, and ensemble decision refinement to capture local and global context in RGB imagery. For hyperspectral data, the proposed HS-SEA architecture introduces a Band Grouping Attention Module (BGAM) and a Spectral-to-Spatial Transfer Gate (SSTG) to exploit spectral-spatial dependencies while efficiently mitigating the Hughes phenomenon. Bayesian optimization is employed to optimize the downstream ensemble classifiers. The proposed framework is validated on nine benchmark datasets, including EuroSAT, NWPU-RESISC45, Bijie Landslide, Turkey Earthquake, MLRSNet, Indian Pines, Salinas, Pavia University, and the recently launched Geology-1 hyperspectral microsatellite dataset. Experimental results show superior classification performance across RGB and hyperspectral modalities, achieving overall accuracies of 6.75% on EuroSAT, 99.28% on NWPU, 93.31% on Bijie Landslide, 98.90% on Turkey Earthquake, 95.00% on MLRSNet, 99.15% on Indian Pines, 99.87% on Salinas, and 99.48% on Pavia University. On the labelscarce Geology-1 dataset, cross-site transfer learning using HS-SEA embeddings and a linear classifier trained on one site achieved 46% and 68% accuracy when transferred to two geographically distinct, unseen sites, demonstrating the framework's ability to generalize to novel, operationally relevant geological hyperspectral data. The results validate the framework's robustness, cross-modality generalization, and discriminative feature-learning effectiveness.

item.title: VLM-Guided Lightweight Multitask Framework for Pine Wilt Disease Quantitative Assessment in UAV Remote Sensing
item.description: Pine wilt disease (PWD) is a highly destructive and contagious forest disease, posing a serious threat to forest ecological security and sustainable forestry development. Under complex stand structures and limited resources, existing methods fail to balance localization accuracy, quantification precision, and semantic understanding of disease distribution. To address this issue, we propose a multitask learning-based model, named PWD multitask network (PWD-MTNet26). Furthermore, a vision-language model-guided semantic-prior enhancement strategy is introduced at training time. By constructing an offline teacher package containing region masks, boundary cues, and confidence information, selective distillation is imposed on the segmentation branch, enabling high-level semantic priors to refine disease-region delineation without increasing inference cost. A joint loss function is constructed to integrate detection and segmentation losses into a unified framework, with optimization conducted at both the pixel and region levels, which improves the recognition of early-stage disease with weak features. Experimental results on real-world datasets show that PWD-MTNet26-SPG achieves 93.5% mAP$_{50}$ for detection and 87.6% mIoU for segmentation. With only 2.5M parameters, the model achieves an inference speed of 84 FPS under the specified hardware and input settings. In the damaged area estimation task, the proposed method outperforms comparative methods across multiple metrics, reducing the normalized root-mean-square error to 0.2197 and the mean absolute error to 1.8149 m$^{2}$, while the damage rate error is only −0.69%.

item.title: The Cooling Effects of Blue-Green Spaces in Arid Oasis Cities from an Energy Balance Perspective: A Case Study of Yinchuan, China
item.description: Blue-green spaces (BGS) provide effective cooling through evapotranspiration, yet the quantitative relationship between latent heat flux (LE) and cooling efficiency remains unclear, particularly in arid urban environments. Here, we quantify the cooling effects associated with instantaneous latent heat flux over BGS and identify critical thresholds governing the Cooling Energy Conversion Rate (CECR). Yinchuan, a typical arid oasis city, was selected as the study area. Multitemporal Landsat data from 2000 to 2025 were used to estimate latent heat flux (LE) based on the two-source energy balance model. Piecewise linear regression combined with partial dependence plots was applied to detect cooling thresholds and quantify CECR. In addition, an XGBoost-SHAP framework was employed to assess the relative contributions of meteorological drivers and spatial morphology of BGS. We demonstrate a significant negative correlation between LE and land surface temperature (LST) (p < 0.05), which supports the cooling effect of LE. The segmented regression further reveals the threshold at which cooling efficiency declines. The identified LE thresholds for vegetation and water bodies are 309.2 W/m2 and 430.0 W/m2, respectively, beyond which further increases in LE are associated with limited additional cooling. The corresponding maximum CECR values are 0.0361°C/(W/m2) for vegetation and 0.0585°C/(W/m2) for water bodies. The contribution of meteorological factors far outweighs that of the spatial morphology of the BGS. Net radiation is the most important predictor, contributing 41.5% and 44.7% to the cooling effects of vegetation and water bodies, respectively. These findings provide a quantitative framework for evaluating the tradeoff between evapotranspiration water(energy) consumption and instantaneous surface cooling benefits of BGS, and offer practical guidance for optimizing urban thermal mitigation strategies in water-limited regions.
